**What type of PR is this?**

/kind bug

<!--

Optionally add one or more of the following kinds if applicable:
/kind api-change
/kind deprecation
/kind failing-test
/kind flake
/kind regression
-->

**What this PR does / why we need it**:

When an apiservice is deleted, its relative `aggregator_unavailable_apiservice` metric remains with the value of the last availability observed. Hence, if an apiservice is deleted while being unavailable, the metric remains marked as unavailable.
This presents some issues when alerting on unavailable apiservices as deleted apiservices might trigger the alert indefinitely.

To solve this issue, the `aggregator_unavailable_apiservice` metric should only reflect the availability of existing apiservices.

This is achievable by using a custom Collector instead of a GaugeVec and create throw-away metrics based on an apiservice lister output. With this approach, on deletion, the apiservice will not be listed anymore, resulting in its availability metric not being exposed.

**Which issue(s) this PR fixes**:
<!--
*Automatically closes linked issue when PR is merged.
Usage: `Fixes #<issue number>`, or `Fixes (paste link of issue)`.
_If PR is about `failing-tests or flakes`, please post the related issues/tests in a comment and do not use `Fixes`_*
-->
Fixes #92671

**Special notes for your reviewer**:

The alert that I previously mentioned is the `AggregatedAPIDown` alert from the kubernetes-mixin project: https://github.com/kubernetes-monitoring/kubernetes-mixin/blob/fe19e65e64183f4a54a4584c792608851f68a1e9/alerts/kube_apiserver.libsonnet#L88-L101
In my opinion, this alert is correct and the problem lies into the `aggregator_unavailable_apiservice` metric which is why I opened this PR.

**Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?**:

-->

```release-note
Fixed a bug where aggregator_unavailable_apiservice metrics were reported for deleted apiservices.
```

comments:
I'm pretty sure that once a given series is created, it cannot be removed. 

cc @logicalhan

Such useless data will generate useless alerts。
I have no choice but to restart kube-apiserver or silences the alerts。
metrics are resettable by sending `DELETE` requests to the `/metrics` endpoint

> metrics are resettable by sending DELETE requests to the /metrics endpoint

Is it possible for the API server to automatically delete specific series when the API objects driving those series are removed?

> metrics are resettable by sending `DELETE` requests to the `/metrics` endpoint

I tried as follows:
1.delete API
```
[root@master ~]# kubectl delete apiservices.apiregistration.k8s.io v1beta1.custom.metrics.k8s.io
apiservice.apiregistration.k8s.io "v1beta1.custom.metrics.k8s.io" deleted
```
2.reset metrics
```
[root@master ~]# curl -XDELETE --cacert /etc/kubernetes/pki/ca.crt -H "Authorization: Bearer `kubectl get secrets default-token-gxdr8 --template={{.data.token}} | base64 -d`" https://10.10.100.150:6443/metrics
metrics reset
```
3.But the series is still
```
[root@master ~]# curl -s --cacert /etc/kubernetes/pki/ca.crt -H "Authorization: Bearer `kubectl get secrets default-token-gxdr8 --template={{.data.token}} | base64 -d`" https://10.10.100.150:6443/metrics | grep "v1beta1.custom.metrics.k8s.io"
aggregator_openapi_v2_regeneration_count{apiservice="v1beta1.custom.metrics.k8s.io",reason="add"} 0
aggregator_openapi_v2_regeneration_count{apiservice="v1beta1.custom.metrics.k8s.io",reason="delete"} 0
aggregator_unavailable_apiservice{name="v1beta1.custom.metrics.k8s.io"} 0
aggregator_unavailable_apiservice_count{name="v1beta1.custom.metrics.k8s.io",reason="MissingEndpoints"} 27
```

> I'm pretty sure that once a given series is created, it cannot be removed.

It is possible to remove a series after creation but this isn't something we currently support as an API.

> metrics are resettable by sending `DELETE` requests to the `/metrics` endpoint

There are some **HUGE** caveats to that statement though.

1. Only a subset of metrics are resettable (and even that subset is not consistent).
2. This is a non-standard, undocumented API which means there is no explicit contract that should allow one to believe this is something one can depend on. 
3. This API is only exposed on apiserver metrics endpoint (where it is undocumented).

Historically, this behavior was snuck in with the [enable-profiling feature](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.18.4/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/server/options/feature.go#L45-L46) (see [also this](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.18.4/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/server/config.go#L701-L703)), which is "supposed" to just enable pprof. 

I suspect it's likely to have been inserted to make perf/scale testing easier but it should not have been exposed like this. This is an unstable, mostly unpredictable (unless you actually read the code), completely undocumented API which you should definitely not be relying on in a production environment. 

> Such useless data will generate useless alerts。
> I have no choice but to restart kube-apiserver or silences the alerts。

It isn't logically necessary for those to be your only two options. I have not seen your alert configuration but from the information that is present to me at this very moment, it is also possible to have a useful alert which doesn't also generate (many) spurious alerts.
What is your alert condition?

> What is your alert condition?

like this: `sum by(name, namespace) (sum_over_time(aggregator_unavailable_apiservice[5m])) > 0`

For example, I created some test API and deleted them after the aggregation failed, but these deleted API will still generate alert
You want to use `rate` here. If your condition is the change in the metric value between some past point and now, then it will only alert for that window of time (events age out of the window).

Thankful.Chang the rules can prevent useless alerts.
bug `rate` calculates the per-second average rate of increase.This calculation method is not suitable for monitoring availability.
e.g.When the metrics value continues to be unavailable within the range of time, the alarm is meaningless.
What makes it not suitable for monitoring availability? I don’t quite understand what you are saying..
Also when I said ‘rate’, I actually meant ‘delta’.

e.g.`aggregator_unavailable_apiservice{name="v1beta1.metrics.k8s.io"}`  The value of this sample is 1 for 5 minutes. Then a promQL like `rate(aggregator_unavailable_apiservice[5m])` cannot accurately indicate whether the API has been successfully aggregated

Use delta. This tells you how much, in the last X minutes, you have increased in your accumulated unavailability. Also, this metric technically never has to tell you if you’re available, it only counts unavailable data points. 

If you use ‘sum’ and compare against a hard coded ‘0’, then you’ve asked for the situation you are encountering, which is fire once and never reset.

`delta` similar.
e.g.
I modified the configuration at 14:30 to make the API aggregation fail
The sample value of my query at 14:34 is not 0, and an alarm is generated at this time. But when the sample value of my query at 14:40 is 0 again, this alart disappears, but in fact, API aggregation still fails.

Ah, I misunderstood which metric you are using in your underlying query, I thought you were using the counter but it sounds like you are alerting off of the gauge. The gauge should indeed update to a zero value (I think) when an aggregation apiservice is deleted. I’ll poke around tomorrow to see why it’s broken.

I am also hitting this issue. Upon an aggregated apiservice deletion, the `aggregator_unavailable_apiservice` gauge is not set to 0.

/remove-lifecycle stale

> I don't think setting the gauge to 0 is the best option we have here. A zero value would mean that the aggregated apiservice is available, which is wrong since it will not exist anymore. This solution would indeed fix the problem we have with the alert firing, but having incorrect information here might be problematic in the future.
> 
> To me, the `aggregator_unavailable_apiservice` metric is like a Prometheus `up` metric and, as such, should follow the same behavior. This means that upon the deletion of its related service, the metric should not exist anymore.
> 
> @logicalhan you mentioned that deleting series is not currently supported by the API. To me knowledge, it should be possible via a custom Collector implementation. Instead of having the availability of the aggregated apiservice in a GaugeVec, we could store this information in a map, and then during collection, manually create the series with `NewLazyConstMetric`. With this implementation, upon deletion, we could delete the apiservice from the map, which will result in its availability not being exposed anymore.

I agree think that after deleting the specified API,the metric should not exist anymore.It is more elegant to let the API delete the series.
